## Triage: **p2** · `bug` · lane **`domain:services`** · `area:workflow` · `pm:queue` (kept) · triage seat · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-19T22:57Z

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015). ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. Fresh read on `origin/main` `191e0430ef`.

**Lane.** `plugin-approvals` is `domain:services` (`SKILL.md:162`). The card carried `pm:queue` with no `domain:*`, so it was unclaimable until now.

**Premise holds.** `rowFromRequest` (`plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`) serves `process_label` (`:1233`), and no `display_title`. So objectui's title ladder falls through to the legacy `titleFormat`: the flow's machine name, then the raw record id.

**Why p2.** It is user-visible on every served approval request page (Setup → Approvals → Requests), and every approver reads it. It is loud and ugly, not wrong data. It also blocks objectui#12484 (p3) under ADR-0060 rule 3.

**Route.** The lane's call. Triage lean: **A1**, the objectui dev's recommendation, at S.
- The get serves `display_title` as the flow label.
- `titleFormat` drops `{record_id}`, or is retired since ADR-0079 already deprecates it.
- The subject stays named by the Details tab's reference card.
- objectui's pin bump then unblocks objectui#12484.

Route ruled by the seat (PM discretion, veto window open): **A1** of the card, under ruling `6190549995` on objectstack-ai/objectui#12438 (letter C keeps the faces "the bare record id is never shown"), ADR-0079 (an explicit `nameField` is the canonical title pointer; `titleFormat` is deprecated) and ADR-0085 (the flow is named by its label, never `flow:NAME`). The mechanism inside A1 is the dev's measured call; the one hard stop is a new key on `ApprovalRequestRow`, which belongs to the spec seat.
